_comment: US HANK two-asset steady state. READ THE `kind` FIELD ON EVERY ROW.
The rows in `targets` are NOT all results. Y, K, r, G, Bg and total
wealth A+B are calibration INPUTS: they are literal entries in the
calibration dictionary, held fixed through the solve, and (Z, alpha,
mu_p, tau, phi) are backed out to make the rest of the model consistent
with them. 'target 10, achieved 10' on capital is a constant equalling
itself; its zero deviation is an identity and carries no information
about whether the model replicates anything. The phrase 'hits every
calibration target' was retired for exactly this reason.
The replication that can fail is in `published_table_b3` below: the
parameters the model solves for INTERNALLY, against the values
Auclert, Bardoczy, Rognlie & Straub (2021), 'Using the Sequence-Space
Jacobian to Solve and Estimate Heterogeneous-Agent Models',
Econometrica 89(5), print in Table B.III. Those had somewhere to miss.
Achieved values in `targets` computed 2026-07-29 by solving the hosted
two-asset model via policyengine_macro.core._hank_solved('two_asset')
(us-hank-model production grids nB=50/nA=70/nK=50); re-solved
independently 2026-08-13 against us-hank-model directly, see
`independent_resolve` below.

_comment: The real replication. These parameters are not imposed: beta and chi1
are solved numerically (chi1 from a 6.5 initial guess), the rest
analytically, from the calibration inputs above. They are compared
against Auclert et al. (2021) Table B.III, which prints 3-4
significant figures. Agreement is to the last published digit on all
six. Recomputed 2026-08-13 by solving us_hank.model.solve_steady_state()
at production grids.

unexplained_discrepancy.name: vphi (wage Phillips curve disutility scale)
unexplained_discrepancy.status: UNRESOLVED and deliberately not asserted in the upstream test suite. This DAG's union_ss block yields 1.7135 where Table B.III publishes 2.073. The implementation is internally self-consistent (wnkpc = 0 at the steady state) and no asset or wealth target depends on it, but asserting a value we cannot reconcile with the paper would launder the discrepancy. It is reported here so the six agreements above are not read as a clean sweep — they are six of seven.

residuals.name: Goods market clearing
residuals.kind: UNTARGETED — holds only by Walras' law, so this is the honest measure of steady-state accuracy

residuals.name: Asset market clearing
residuals.kind: SOLVER TARGET — this is the tolerance the root-finder converged to, not an accuracy. Quoting it as the model's precision would overstate it by roughly five orders of magnitude.

independent_resolve.method: us_hank.model.solve_steady_state() run directly against a us-hank-model checkout (US_HANK_MODEL, default ~/us-hank-model) at production grids, outside the hosted adapter
independent_resolve.note: Reproduces every value above. The two market-clearing residuals land at 3.197e-13 (asset) and 3.294e-08 (goods) rather than the 3.126e-13 / 3.294e-08 recorded on 2026-07-29 — run-to-run variation at the solver tolerance, which is itself a reason not to read the asset-market figure as a precision claim. The 2026-07-29 values are kept as the record rather than overwritten.

beta_note: beta is one of the two numerically solved parameters, not a free knob tuned to the wealth targets: the wealth targets are inputs, and beta is what the household block requires to be consistent with them. Its independent content is that the paper reports 0.976 and this implementation returns 0.9762739.
